title: Louisville roadhouse and the Roseland Ballroom in Lexington
summary: A $25 a week roadhouse job on the Ohio River keeps the band together until they book Lexington dances and win a job at the Roseland Ballroom.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: It's up on the Ohio River, this roadhouse. And we took this job and back in those days, you know, that was during the days of Prohibition -- people'd come out and they would eat and, of course, whether they were serving liquor, I don't know, but they -- they were drinking at the tables, you know what I mean, you see? And the job paid us $25.00 a week. And that little job kept us together when we got in Louisville for a few weeks.

So we decided to book some dates in Lexington, Kentucky. And this we did. We booked our band in Lexington, Kentucky, and we played a big dance there and the band was such a big riot, you know, so we booked another date there, I think, about 10 days later. Well the owners of the Roseland Ballroom had heard about us and they came out and heard the band. They heard the band and they offered us a job. Working at this ballroom in Lexington. And this must've been latter part of November, I guess, in November.
